candidates.statement: a. Investigators should comply with the standard practice of obtaining a fungal 104 smear and culture on all clinically relevant samples. All positive and negative 105 results should be documented on case report forms and included in the datasets. 106 This is especially important for BAL samples so that the presence of Aspergillus 107 species or rare fungal pathogens (such as Penicillium, Paecilomyces, 108 Geotrichum, and Histoplasma) that may cross-react with the galactomannan 109 assay are documented. 110

candidates.statement: The data to support qualification were obtained with use of the Bio-Rad Platelia Aspergillus EIA. 140 The criteria for a positive galactomannan index described here for use in investigational studies 141 of treatments for IA are different from the FDA-cleared Bio-Rad Platelia Aspergillus EIA device 142 labeling. The recommendations of this guidance do not alter the labeling recommendations of the 143 galactomannan assay for use in the medical care of patients, and cut-off values specified in the 144 device labeling should continue to be used. The use of different criteria for research is to 145 increase the positive predictive value of the Bio-Rad Platelia Aspergillus EIA. 146
candidates.context: Section II: Supportive Information 138 Section III: Performance Characteristics of the Assay for the Qualification of 148 Galactomannan 149

candidates.statement: Sponsors using non-FDA-cleared galactomannan assays for studies to be submitted 162 within a drug development regulatory submission to FDA should determine the 163 performance characteristics of the assay using clinical studies to assess performance 164 against defined reference standards and should ensure that the assay is adequate for the 165 COU. For this performance assessment, analytical parameters such as precision, 166 reproducibility, and cross-reaction with non- Aspergillus fungal species should be 167 determined. Sponsors should discuss their plans with FDA prior to conducting clinical 168 studies. 169
